title: Correction #2: Where Zones Begin
hook: There are two corrections in the sequence. Only the second one creates the zone.

launchpad.outcome: Tell Correction #1 from Correction #2, and explain why Correction #2 is where the zone begins.
launchpad.missionQuestion: Why does the zone come from Correction #2 and not Correction #1?

takeaways: Correction #1 comes after BOS #1. Correction #2 comes after BOS #2.
A zone from Correction #2 is only potential until BOS #3 occurs.
If BOS #3 never happens, there’s no trade.

slides.headline: Two corrections. Only one makes the zone.
slides.line: After BOS #2 (the second break of structure), price pulls back again. That second pullback is where the zone begins.

slides.headline: Correction #1 ≠ Correction #2.
slides.line: They look alike on a chart. What sets them apart is where they sit in the sequence.

versus.label: Correction #1
points: It moves preferably back toward the original 15M break.

versus.label: Correction #2
points: It creates the supply or demand zone.
Its zone stays potential until BOS #3.

slides.kicker: Step 2 · Both corrections on a chart
slides.headline: Count the pullbacks: first, then second.
slides.line: Bullish example. Press the button to print each part.

steps.caption: Correction #1. The first 5M pullback, right after BOS #1. It doesn’t create the zone.
BOS #2. A 5M close above the high Correction #1 pulled back from. Now watch for the next pullback.
Correction #2. The second pullback, after BOS #2. This is where the zone begins.

slides.headline: Both corrections are here. Find the second.
slides.line: Bearish example. BOS #1 and BOS #2 are marked. In a bearish model, the corrections bounce up.
slides.why: That candle is in the pullback after BOS #2. That’s Correction #2, and it’s where the supply zone will come from.

after.caption: Correction #1 came after BOS #1. Correction #2 came after BOS #2. Correction #2 creates the zone.

slides.headline: Correction #2 is here. Can you trade it yet?
slides.line: Bullish model. Correction #2 just printed its last bearish candle.

check.prompt: Is the demand zone ready to trade?

options.label: Yes, the bearish candle has appeared
options.feedback: Not yet. A zone isn’t activated just because the opposite-colour candle appeared. BOS #3 must occur.

options.label: No, it’s a potential zone until BOS #3
options.why: Right. Correction #2 creates the zone, and BOS #3 activates it.

slides.kicker: Step 5 · A zone that never activates
slides.headline: Correction #2 forms. BOS #3 doesn’t.
slides.line: Bullish example. Watch what happens after Correction #2.

steps.caption: Correction #1, BOS #2, then Correction #2. Correction #2 leaves a potential demand zone.
No 5M candle closes above the high Correction #2 pulled back from. BOS #3 never happens, so the zone never activates.

check.prompt: Correction #2 made a potential zone, but BOS #3 never came. What do you do?

options.label: Buy when price comes back to the zone
options.feedback: This zone was never activated. A zone needs BOS #3 before the entry model applies.

options.label: No trade, the sequence is incomplete
options.why: Right. Without BOS #3 the zone stays potential, and there’s no trade.

slides.quote: The first pullback gets you ready. The second one builds the zone.

slides.prompt: In your own words, how do you tell Correction #1 from Correction #2, and what does Correction #2 do?
slides.modelAnswer: Correction #1 is the first 5M pullback, after BOS #1. Correction #2 is the second 5M pullback, after BOS #2. Correction #2 creates the zone, but that zone is only potential until BOS #3 occurs. If BOS #3 never happens, there’s no trade.
